source.title: Entropy-SGD optimizes the prior of a PAC-Bayes bound: Data-dependent PAC-Bayes priors via differential privacy

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; figures are text-extracted, with some plotted values not numerically recoverable.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly measures training error under SGD, SGLD, Entropy-SGD, and Entropy-SGLD, including random labels, and reports cases of overfitting or increased training error as noise changes. Its focus is generalization bounds, but these are its own training-error results relevant to V1.
record.gate_note: Reports training-error outcomes for learned networks and Gibbs classifiers on MNIST and CIFAR10. Numerical values in several plots are not recoverable from the text; cited results from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study measures training classification error, including fitting random labels, using alternative gradient-based training methods. Its CIFAR10 experiments bear directly on V1; convolutional MNIST experiments extend the question to another dataset. It does not test V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly correct, but the speed comparison should be corrected: the authors explicitly say Entropy-SGLD learns much more slowly than Entropy-SGD. They conclude that Entropy-SGD can overfit, privacy-tuned Entropy-SGLD can control overfitting, and its tighter generalization bounds remain optimistic because convergence is assumed. Performance remains below SGD, suggesting a possible tradeoff among speed, excess risk, and certifiable generalization.
record.recipe_differences: Studies variants of SGD and Entropy-SGD, including added outer-loop SGLD noise and bounded cross-entropy, on MNIST and CIFAR10; not a direct reproduction of the cataloged gradient-training claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Thermal noise, τ, γ, dataset label type, and architecture affect risk/training error or generalization behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Fully connected MNIST networks have similar train and test errors; FC1024 shows approximately 2% random-label overfitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Privacy-tuned Entropy-SGLD can suppress memorization in fully connected MNIST networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix C.1 reports similar generalization bounds with and without batch normalization and says removing it requires learning-rate tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch normalization changes learning-rate tuning requirements in these SGLD experiments.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 35th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 80, 2018
record.problems: Many training-error values are shown only in figures and are not numerically recoverable from the text. Experiments concern two-class and multiclass MNIST and CIFAR10, not CIFAR-100. The paper notes optimistic bounds based on an assumption that SGLD has converged and does not include Monte Carlo error in one reported estimate.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. CIFAR10 Figure 5 sweep values remain figure-only because precise plotted values are not stated in the text.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100; ordinary SGD or Adam fitting CIFAR10 in this study; systematic model-size and early-stopping comparisons; a controlled random-initialization comparison. MNIST results extend beyond the datasets named in V1.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious-minimum frequencies, and extra-student-neuron comparisons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and identity-shortcut comparisons.
Initialization-dependent training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to a measured stability threshold, curvature dynamics, and edge-of-stability behavior.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and tolerated learning rates; Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: The abstract explicitly reports zero random-label training error for available Entropy-SGD implementations and their Gibbs posterior. Add a result distinguishing deterministic and Gibbs classifiers and recover the applicable experimental conditions; R5 currently records only unspecified overfitting.
missing.versions: V1, as an extension beyond ordinary SGD

record.verdict_notes: MNIST convolutional results are treated as extensions of V1, not direct CIFAR replications. Fully connected results do not test the specified convolutional claim. Generalization gap, test error, and training error must remain distinct. Privacy-tuned failures to memorize do not challenge V1's ordinary-SGD assertion. Figure-only values were not reconstructed.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100 and smaller-model comparisons are not reported. Results for random labels and early stopping are limited to the stated tested settings; no systematic early-stopping comparison is described.

rows.subject: CONV

rows.note: The text says both mean and Gibbs classifiers have essentially zero generalization error; it does not separately give a numeric training-error value here. Figure plots training error.
rows.check: The essentially-zero quantity is the generalization gap, not training error. Approximately 2% test error with essentially zero gap implies approximately 2% training error for both mean and Gibbs classifiers; distinguish these subjects.
